ops.title: Flaky: TestDiscoverTimeoutKillsDescendants races three wall-clock deadlines
ops.description:
`TestDiscoverTimeoutKillsDescendants` (`internal/codeexec/discover_test.go:198`) fails under load and passes when the box is quiet.

It spawns a TERM-ignoring fake `claude`, sets `CCX_EXEC_MCP_TIMEOUT=500ms`, then races three wall-clock deadlines: 500ms for the timeout to fire, 2s to read the grandchild PID file, and 3s for the grandchild to die. On a loaded machine — observed with the full module running under `-race` alongside two wasm rebuilds — those budgets slip and the test goes red.

Established as a flake rather than a regression: re-run 4× immediately afterwards (plain ×2, `-race` ×1, whole `internal/codeexec` package under `-race` ×1, 23.2s) and green every time. Also green in the pre-change baseline and in two earlier full runs of the same tree.

Unrelated to the open-pr change set — `internal/codeexec` is the `ccx exec` sandbox engine and shares no code with `internal/cli`'s ship path. Deliberately left untouched so the review lane wasn't handed unrelated surface to read.

The fix is timing robustness in the test: derive the budgets from the configured timeout rather than pinning absolute wall-clock seconds, or poll with a generous ceiling instead of a fixed sleep. Worth noting that the same class of bug — a wall-clock assertion that only holds on an idle machine — showed up in the ship probe's timeout test during this work, where an unnoticed version of it made the test pass in 0.09s while asserting nothing.

ops.text: The test derives its deadlines from CCX_EXEC_MCP_TIMEOUT rather than pinning absolute wall-clock seconds, or polls to a generous ceiling
It passes with the full module running concurrently under -race
